thread:
incident-bot: PAGER: GPU-SCHEDULER-HIGH-QUEUE — queue depth exceeded threshold on us-west-2-gpu-cluster. auto-escalate to oncall
kevin.sun: got it, I'm awake. pulling metrics now.
kevin.sun: grafana shows queued_requests = 920 -> 1.2k in last 20m, p95 gen latency 3.6s -> 12s.
eng-sre: seeing repeated allocation failures from scheduler: 
```
E allocation failed: no compatible node (fragmentation: required 1g slice contiguous, only 7g+ slices available)
E candidate nodes filtered by mig-profile mismatch
```

michael_t: autoscaler tried to scale but kept hitting cloud provider quota/placement failures. cloud api returned some partial capacity but pods stayed Pending.
kevin.sun: quick summary: autoscaler issued scale up -> new nodes created with MIG configuration 1xA100-7g (expected), but scheduler requires contiguous slices matching requested MIG sizes for inference pods so many new nodes accepted only small slices leaving existing large-slice nodes stranded. net result = stranded GPU capacity + pending queue.
irene: customers reporting degraded throughput. cs-rep: flagged 3 enterprise tenants with timeouts and increased error rates. CS outreach in progress.
kevin.sun: initial mitigation idea: 1) relax strict mig-slice matching in scheduler to allow multi-slice packing, 2) force rebalancing/drain of fragmented nodes, 3) temporarily allow fallback to lower-capacity model variant on heavy routes.
sana.lee: before we change scheduler rules, can we try a targeted drain+recreate to free contiguous slices? which nodes are worst?
eng-sre: list from placement logs: problematic nodes: gpu-node-uw2-45, gpu-node-uw2-47, gpu-node-uw2-61. They each have mixed leftover 1x40g + 2x7g leftovers causing packing holes. Estimated stranded GPUs = 12 (3 nodes * 4 slices).
kevin.sun: I'm going to start cordon+drain of gpu-node-uw2-61 and recreate with uniform MIG split 4x7g to match our workload. doing it now.
kevin.sun: run: 
```
kubectl cordon gpu-node-uw2-61
kubectl drain gpu-node-uw2-61 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force
cloudctl compute instance recreate --node gpu-node-uw2-61 --mig-split 4x7g
```
kevin.sun: drain succeeded, pods evicted, several pods rescheduled to other nodes and some pending due to shortage. recreating node now.
eng-sre: while that runs, I'm toggling a temporary autoscaler policy to allow a 15% burst above commit so we can absorb the queue if cloud will provide capacity. toggled.
deply-bot: deploy-bot: autoscaler-policy updated (burst_allowed=true).
kevin.sun: new node came up with 4x7g. scheduler placed 6 waiting pods onto it. queued_requests down to 540.
kevin.sun: repeat for gpu-node-uw2-45 next.
michael_t: note — cloud provider returned intermittent 429s earlier; we saw partial create success where nodes were created but had mixed MIG default. we need a longer term fix in cluster image to ensure consistent MIG split template.
irene: customer impact update: CS reached out to the three flagged tenants. one reported 30% request failures during incident window. apologies sent and incident ticket opened.
eng-sre: while manual drains are helping, fragmentation still causing small pockets of stranded capacity. proposing: short-term scheduler patch to relax exact-mig-match for our inference pods and allow multi-slice placement (best-effort), with a feature-flag.
sana.lee: can we gate this behind feature-flag + rate limit so we don't over-pack and cause perf regressions?
kevin.sun: yes. I'll push a hotfix to the scheduler: change placement predicate from exactSliceMatch -> allowMultiSlicePack if node has X free slices. rolling it to staging then canary to us-west-2-gpu-cluster.
kevin.sun: hotfix PR: 
```
// sched/placement/predicate.go
- if !ExactMigMatch(req, node) { reject }
+ if FeatureFlag("allowMultiSlicePack") && MultiSliceAcceptable(req, node) { accept }
```
kevin.sun: promoting to canary in cluster now.
eng-sre: canary applied to subset of scheduling replicas. watching.
kevin.sun: canary picked up pending pods and placed 42 more allocations across fragmented nodes. queued_requests down to 90. p95 latency back to ~3.8s.
michael_t: great. things stabilizing. keep monitoring for 30m and then we can lift emergency policies.
cs-rep: sent status update to affected customers: summary + ETA for root cause / postmortem. one requested SLA credit evaluation.
sana.lee: oncall handoff in ~45m. I'll take night shift. summary for handoff:
- root cause: MIG fragmentation + strict scheduler MIG-match predicate prevented binpacking -> autoscaler scaleups created nodes with incompatible slices leaving stranded GPUs.
- mitigations applied: manual drain/recreate of 3 nodes (freed 12 slices), temporary autoscaler burst enabled, scheduler canary feature-flag allowMultiSlicePack rolled to canary and accepted pending pods, traffic fallback enabled for a few routes.
- impact: ~3 customers with increased errors; queue peak ~1.2k; total incident duration (so far) ~2h.
- next steps: postmortem owner: eng-runtime (michael_t), scheduled RCA meeting tomorrow 11am.
kevin.sun: leaving detailed runbook edits in #eng-oncall-runbooks. Added script to detect fragmentation: 
```
#!/bin/bash
# detect nodes with mixed mig slices
kubectl get nodes -l gpu=true -o json | jq '.items[] | {name:.metadata.name, mig: .metadata.annotations.mig_split}'
```
sana.lee: thanks. I'll monitor overnight, keep burst_allow true for now. escalate to infra if autoscaler hits provider quota.
michael_t: assigning post-incident tasks: 1) scheduler long-term change — support relaxed packing with perf safeguards; 2) admission/launch templates — enforce consistent MIG split on node bootstrap; 3) autoscaler safety — detect fragmentation and prefer recreate over blind scale.
eng-sre: tagging incident severity SEV2 and creating incident channel for postmortem notes.
cs-rep: closing customer notifications for now; will update after postmortem.
kevin.sun: thanks team. nice quick coordination. handing off to @sana.lee for night watch. :thumbsup:
sana.lee: acknowledged, taking handoff. I'll post an update if anything changes.
incident-bot: INCIDENT: work-in-progress -> mitigated (monitoring).
